correctness.rationale: A graph defined on twelve ordered pairs has exactly 48 connected and 447 disconnected induced four-sets. The full Alexander dual has face vector (12,66,220,48), not merely the closure of the 48 tetrahedra. An explicit 48-pair simplicial-collapse certificate leaves a 2-complex with f=(12,66,172); an eleven-edge tree and 55 checked triangular relations kill all 55 non-tree edge generators, proving pi_1=0. Reduced Euler characteristic 117 and free H_2 imply a wedge of 117 two-spheres; the cut complex contains the complete six-skeleton, and integral Alexander duality, Hurewicz and Whitehead give a wedge of 117 seven-spheres. Signed face-trace computations over all 24 group elements give the character and its five irreducible multiplicities. All enumerated premises replayed from the included actual files.

value.rationale: The truncated tetrahedron is a canonical twelve-vertex Archimedean cubic graph with full S4 symmetry and four triangles. Its four-cut topology is not covered by the girth-five theorem, and its already classified three-cut topology cannot decide the next cut stage. The complete integral homotopy type, 117-sphere rank, and all five rational character values, especially the eight invariant classes, provide a coherent natural finite classification and a reproducible low-girth comparison, not an arbitrary parameter slice or bare known Euler count.
